Decision-engine architecture and invariants

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Explain the pure deterministic core
  • Map INV, DEC and SEC obligations
  • Recognise policy that belongs outside workflow code

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01Decision contract
  2. 02Typed model
  3. 03Compiled expression
  4. 04Pure evaluation
  5. 05Outcome + trace
  6. 06Invariant tests

1. A separate policy plane

The Rust workspace is the deterministic policy brain. Workflow gathers canonical facts and asks a named decision; policy does not leak into route-level conditionals.

2. Load-bearing invariants

Evaluation has no clock, randomness or I/O, uses exact decimals, produces stable trace lineage and fails closed. The design document's INV, DEC and SEC identifiers are test obligations, not commentary.

3. Crate boundaries

Core contracts, expressions, models, compilation, evaluation, bundles, governance, providers and service adapters remain separated so pure evaluation crates do not acquire network or async dependencies.
